title: Buy the field (Jeremiah 32)
hook: as Jerusalem falls, Jeremiah buys a field as a sign that people will return
carry: plant the tree, sign the lease

segments.voice: Yesterday, a new covenant: not on stone tablets this time, but a line no exile can carry off. Did one line stay with you all day without a page in front of you? Today, a promise gets written into a deed and sealed in a jar. Day eight hundred seven.
screen: `A LINE NO EXILE CAN CARRY OFF.`

segments.voice: The army of Babylon is camped around Jerusalem. Jeremiah is locked in the court of the prison, because the king doesn't like what he keeps saying: that the city will fall. And then his cousin Hanamel shows up with a business offer. He has a field back home in Anathoth, the family land, and by the law of the family, Jeremiah has the right to redeem it. Buy my field, he says. It is a strange thing to be sold. The land is about to be in enemy hands. The seller knows it. The buyer knows it. The buyer is in jail. And Jeremiah says yes.
screen: `BABYLON AROUND THE WALLS.` → `THE PROPHET IN PRISON.` → `A COUSIN SELLING A FIELD.`

segments.voice: Jeremiah does the whole deal properly. He weighs out the silver, seventeen shekels, the text says. He signs the deed, seals it, calls witnesses. There are two copies, one sealed and one left open. Then he hands them to his scribe, Baruch, in front of everyone in the prison court, and tells him to put both copies in an earthen jar, so they will last a long time. Why the fuss? Because this is not really a purchase. It's a sign. Jeremiah says out loud what it means, and in the King James words it is this: "Houses and fields and vineyards shall be possessed again in this land." People will buy and sell here again. Deeds will be signed here again. Life will come back. And here is the human part. Right after the deal, Jeremiah prays, and in his prayer he admits that the siege mounds are already at the walls. He did the right thing, and he still seems unsure. The answer comes back as a question: "Behold, I am the LORD, the God of all flesh: is there any thing too hard for me?" Then the promise is repeated, almost word for word: fields shall be bought in this land. Notice the order. The hope isn't a feeling first and an action after. Jeremiah pays first. The silver leaves his hand while the city is still under siege. A hope that costs something, and gets written down, and gets sealed in a jar for later. Some readers take it as a picture of a hopeful act when nothing around it looks hopeful: plant the tree, sign the lease, put the deed in the jar.
screen: `SILVER WEIGHED, DEED SEALED.` · `TWO COPIES IN AN EARTHEN JAR.` · then, large: `FIELDS SHALL BE POSSESSED AGAIN.` · then: `IS ANY THING TOO HARD FOR ME?` · `PAY FIRST, WHILE THE CITY IS BESIEGED.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: invest in one hope. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind something that seems unlikely right now. A friendship that cooled. A town that's struggling. A plan you shelved. Something in your own life that looks besieged. Don't fix it. Just ask: what would one small down payment look like? A message. A seed in a pot. Five dollars toward something. A date on the calendar. Let one answer come, and hold it, the way Jeremiah held the deed before he handed it to Baruch. If you pray, you can bring that hope before God. The bell holds the time.
Anathoth, Jeremiah's family land, which he bought from prison as a sign that Babylon's siege wouldn't be the end. Today's word.
Your line: plant the tree, sign the lease. Today, make the small down payment you found in the sit, before you feel sure. Day eight hundred seven.

howItsDone: Jews read Jeremiah 32:6–27 as the haftarah for the Torah portion Behar, which sets out the law of redeeming family land, and the purchase at Anathoth is often taught as a picture of acting on hope during disaster.

fork.setup: you're Jeremiah, in prison, and the city is about to fall. your cousin offers you the family field. what do you do?
options: say no: the land is lost anyway.
buy it, with witnesses and a sealed deed.
promise to buy it after the war.
fork.reveal: he buys it at once, weighs the silver, seals the deed, and has it stored in a jar: a sign that fields will be bought in this land again.

original.note: Hebrew: field, the land Jeremiah buys in Anathoth.

trapdoor: what you thought: a prophet makes a bad investment.
what it means: the purchase is a sign that life will return to the land.
what a scholar hears: the deed is sealed, witnessed and stored in a jar, a hope made legal and put away for later.

notes: Quotations are KJV; Keeper may prefer JPS 1917 wording (JPS 32:15 reads closer to 'shall yet again be bought').
'By the law of the family' summarizes the right of redemption in Jeremiah 32:7–8; Keeper may want to name the law (Leviticus 25).
'Some readers take it as a picture of a hopeful act' is a deliberately soft framing.
Editor: cut the unsourced superlative 'the worst real estate pitch in the Bible'; review line now says the promise is written into a deed, not on paper.
